about.title: About Ovulation Calculator - Fertility Tracking Tool
about.description: The Ovulation Calculator estimates fertile days based on menstrual cycle length and last period date. Understanding the ovulation window can support family planning and cycle-awareness workflows. Ovulation often occurs 12-16 days before the next period, but timing can vary. This calculator helps outline a possible fertile window and provides reference information for reproductive health planning.

howTo.title: How to Use the Ovulation Calculator

steps.title: Enter Last Period Date
steps.description: Input the first day of your last menstrual period using the date picker.

steps.title: Set Cycle Length
steps.description: Enter your average cycle length (typically 21-35 days, average 28 days).

steps.title: View Ovulation Date
steps.description: See an estimated ovulation date based on your cycle pattern.

steps.title: Check Fertile Window
steps.description: Review the estimated 6-day fertile window for planning and awareness.

steps.title: Track Multiple Cycles
steps.description: Monitor patterns over several cycles for more useful comparison and planning.

steps.title: Plan Accordingly
steps.description: Use the information for family planning or fertility awareness.

faq.q: How should I interpret ovulation predictions?
faq.a: Predictions are cycle-based estimates and actual ovulation timing can vary due to stress, illness, or hormonal changes. Use the results as a planning reference rather than a certainty, and consult a healthcare provider for medical guidance.

faq.q: What is the fertile window and why is it 6 days?
faq.a: The fertile window is the 6-day period when pregnancy is possible - 5 days before ovulation plus ovulation day. Sperm can survive up to 5 days in the female reproductive tract, while the egg is viable for about 24 hours after ovulation.

faq.q: Can I use this calculator for birth control?
faq.a: This calculator is for educational and awareness purposes only and should not be relied upon as a sole method of contraception. The fertility awareness method requires additional tracking. Consult healthcare providers for reliable birth control options.

faq.q: What if my cycles are irregular?
faq.a: Irregular cycles can make cycle-based estimates less consistent because ovulation timing may vary. Track multiple cycles, note any patterns, and consider consulting a healthcare provider for individualized guidance on fertility timing and possible underlying causes.
